title: Short Stuff: The Zipper Merge
summary: Short Stuff episode on the zipper merge, the traffic technique of staying in a closing lane until the last possible moment and then alternating with through-lane traffic. Josh and Chuck explain why merging early causes slowdowns and bumper-to-bumper traffic, and why American drivers often resist it because it feels like cutting in line. They discuss German usage (Reißverschlussverfahren), driving experiences in Australia and Canada, state signage campaigns urging both lanes to merge, Illinois making blocking a zipper merge finable, and the hosts' pledge to zipper merge. The episode closes with Josh's joke about the origin of the name, which is a crude remark about the orange cones.

segments.title: Opening banter and highway sign scenario
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the topic with a scenario about a lane closure sign on the highway and the problem of drivers rushing to merge early.

segments.title: What zipper merging is
segments.summary: Josh defines zipper merging as staying in a closing lane until the last possible moment and then alternating with traffic in the through lane. Early merging causes a slowdown. Chuck says Americans don't take turns, and mentions the German term Reißverschlussverfahren.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break with a short show tease.

segments.title: Why early merging causes slowdowns
segments.summary: Josh explains that early merging by drivers in the closing lane creates a bumper-to-bumper slowdown and unfair advantage. Chuck asks about data on congestion reduction and whether the zipper merge is effective at high speed.

segments.title: Drivers in the through lane and merging courtesy
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss what drivers in the through lane should do when people merge around them, such as slowing to let someone in or moving over to create space. Chuck admits he used to merge early and now waits.

segments.title: Why Americans merge early: cutting in line
segments.summary: Josh explains that early merging feels fair to many American drivers but is seen as cutting in line, which angers people, and mentions the rarity but reality of road rage.

segments.title: Driving habits in other countries and road behavior
segments.summary: Chuck describes civil driving he experienced in Australia and New Zealand, Josh says Canada is similar, and they discuss American road anger. Chuck mentions state signage and education campaigns.

segments.title: Illinois law and phone use while driving
segments.summary: Josh says some states, including Illinois, have made blocking a zipper merge punishable by a fine. They briefly discuss drivers on phones and recommend using extra signs saying use both lanes to merge.

segments.title: Hosts pledge to zipper merge and name origin joke
segments.summary: Chuck says he will zipper merge from now on. Josh jokes about how the name came about, comparing an orange cone in the merge to something crude.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Brief closing and iHeartRadio production credit.
